summary: Red Seal describes Industrial Mechanic (Millwright) work as covering industrial machinery and mechanical equipment including pneumatic/hydraulic systems, conveyors, robotics and automated equipment. Use it to ground trade scope and competency vocabulary, not project geometry.

Skilled Trades Ontario describes the Ontario 433A trade and training areas including drawings/schematics, power transmission, electrical/electronic controls, pneumatics/hydraulics, predictive maintenance, welding, machining and equipment bases.

ISO 12100 provides the general machinery-design risk-assessment and risk-reduction framework across machine life-cycle phases. The full copyrighted standard is not stored by this service unless separately licensed/provided.
PMMI identifies ANSI/PMMI B155.1 as applying to new, modified or rebuilt packaging machinery, including conveying machinery within packaging functions and coordinated packaging-line functions.
ISA publishes consensus standards and guidance for industrial automation and control systems. This source is a discovery anchor for control, commissioning, documentation and automation practice.
ISA-5 provides standardized instrumentation/control symbols, identification and documentation conventions that help engineers, technicians and operators communicate consistently.
CEMA is an ANSI-accredited standards developer for conveyor equipment and maintains consensus standards addressing conveyor terminology, design, manufacture and application.

NFPA 79 is the Electrical Standard for Industrial Machinery and addresses electrical equipment across industrial machines, including complex automated manufacturing systems. Store metadata/public scope only unless licensed.

AWS develops welding codes and standards covering welding procedure/welder qualification, fabrication, inspection and acceptance. Exact applicability depends on material, structure and project specification.
SMRP organizes maintenance and reliability knowledge into business/management, manufacturing process reliability, equipment reliability, organization/leadership and work management pillars.

Festo's pneumatics training covers compressed-air supply, actuators, directional/flow/pressure control valves, sensors, circuit diagrams, operating modes, safety and fault finding. Treat vendor training as professional practice, not project-specific authority.

Sandvik Coromant's metal-cutting training covers machinability, turning, parting/grooving, threading, milling, drilling, boring and toolholding, useful for manufacturability and machining-practice review.

Eng-Tips mechanical discussions include practitioner questions about mechanisms, bearings, tolerances and current roller-carriage concepts. Use posts to surface failure modes and tests; never treat forum consensus as verification.

Eng-Tips industrial/manufacturing forums cover automation/robotics, machines/machining, plant engineering, QC/inspection and manufacturing practice, including real-world conveyor/orientation questions.

PLCtalk contains large practitioner discussions across PLCs/IPCs, networking, HMI/SCADA, motion/motor control, hardware, programming and troubleshooting. It is useful for commissioning patterns and failure hypotheses only.

Control.com hosts practitioner forums for motion control, instrumentation, electrical engineering, safety and general automation; current discussions include packaging-line actuator selection. Use as chatter, not engineering authority.

SMRP Exchange is a practitioner discussion surface for maintenance/reliability topics such as asset obsolescence and lifecycle practice. Community discussion remains distinct from the formal SMRP Body of Knowledge.

Machinist community discussions frequently expose shop-floor concerns about drawing clarity, realistic tolerances, setup effort and cost. Treat these as practical hypothesis prompts and manufacturability questions only.
